observation.visible_scene: A low-angle upward view through the canopy of a leafy tree (broad, glossy green leaves with a few yellowing ones) against a pale blue sky with thin clouds. A single white open flower sits near the top-center, framed by branches, and a thin bare twig hangs down in the central sky gap. The foliage forms a rough ring around the open sky in the middle of the frame.
visible_changes: The overall composition is essentially static across the excerpt: the white flower, the central bare twig, and the leaf clusters keep the same positions relative to the frame edges from the first to the last sampled frame.

A small bright specular sun-glint appears on the right-side leaves around the middle of the segment (roughly t≈0.27–0.5s) and then fades, consistent with a reflection moving on/off a leaf surface rather than a separate object.
No clear translation, expansion, or deformation of the main branches or the flower is supported by the frames; the changes are limited to the transient highlight and negligible, if any, leaf motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the camera or leaves move outside this cropped window, and the cause of the brief highlight (sun-angle shift vs. a leaf moving into the light).
The wider tree, ground, or sky context beyond the frame edges.
uncertain_details: Any very slight camera drift or gentle leaf sway cannot be reliably distinguished from static framing at this sampling rate.
The exact timing of the highlight's appearance/disappearance is approximate given the discrete frames.

NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
